title: MyLinden Help: Automatic Debit on Patient Payment Plans
content:
Automatic debit on a Patient Payment Plans installment plan is either required or optional depending on the tier, and each tier sets how a failed debit is retried and how many returned debits end automatic debit.

**Which tiers require automatic debit?**

| Tier | Installments must be paid by automatic debit | Days after a failed debit before it is retried | Retries of a failed debit | Returned debits after which automatic debit is removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Interest-Free Plan | No | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| 6-Month Interest-Free Plan | No | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| 12-Month Interest-Free Plan | Yes | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| 18-Month Extended Plan | Yes | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| 24-Month Extended Plan | Yes | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| Financial Hardship Plan | No | 5 | 1 | 2 |

**What happens when a debit fails?** A failed automatic debit is retried the number of times shown, the number of calendar days apart shown; after its retries the installment is left to the grace period. On every tier there is 1 retry; it follows 3 calendar days after the failure, or 5 calendar days on the Financial Hardship Plan.

**When is automatic debit taken off the plan?** After 2 returned automatic debits on any tier, automatic debit is removed and the patient pays each installment manually.

**A hypothetical example.** On an 18-Month Extended Plan whose debit fails on the 12th of a month, the single retry falls 3 calendar days later, on the 15th. On a Financial Hardship Plan paid by automatic debit, a debit failing on the 12th is retried on the 17th.
